title: Annotatio IV §.XIII: Bertram — not corporal/oral eating; spiritual presence and participation (SPIRITUALE CORPUS)
pass_a_gloss: (III) And about to prove that Christ’s natural body is not eaten Corporally or Orally in the Supper, he proposes this question expressly: Whether the very body born of Mary and that suffered, died and was buried, and that sits at the Father’s Right Hand, is what is taken daily by the Faithful’s mouth through the mystery of the Sacraments in the Church? And he answers from Ambrose speaking through Scripture… Not according to this which is seen, which is taken corporally, which is pressed by the tooth, which is swallowed by the throat… does it supply the substance of eternal life… Meanwhile yet (IV.) about to confess with full mouth both the Spiritual presence and the participation of Christ’s body, occupied in the Response to the Emperor’s prior question — Whether in some Mysterious mode Christ’s body is taken by the Faithful in the Supper? — he answers among other things thus: Since by all’s confession the body and blood of Christ are taken in the Supper, it is necessary that bread and wine have passed into something better, and that this mutation has happened not CORPORALLY but SPIRITUALLY, so that now it is rightly said the said mutation was made FIGURATIVELY, and under the covering of corporal bread and wine the SPIRITUAL BODY AND SPIRITUAL BLOOD of Christ are actually present… Because it is SPIRITUAL FOOD, it is SPIRITUAL DRINK, feeding spiritually and granting the life of eternal satiety.
pass_b_english: Bertram (III): the body born of Mary, dead, risen, at the Father’s right, is not what teeth press and throats swallow daily — that corporal intake does not supply eternal life.

(IV) Yet he confesses Spiritual presence and participation: bread and wine pass into something better not CORPORALLY but SPIRITUALLY — under corporal covering the SPIRITUAL BODY AND BLOOD are actually present; SPIRITUAL FOOD and DRINK.
source_text: (III) Nec naturale corpus Christi, Corporaliter, seu Oraliter, in Cœna manducari evicturus, quæstionem hanc ex professo proponit: Utrum ipsum corpus quod de Maria natum & passum, mortuum & sepultum, quodque ad Dextram Patris residet, sit, quod ore Fidelium per Sacramentorum mysterium, in Ecclesia quotidie sumatur? Et respondet ex Ambrosio per Scripturam loquente… Non secundum hoc, quod videtur, quod corporaliter sumitur, quod dente premitur, quod fauce glutitur… æterna vita substantiam subministrat… Interim tamen (IV.) Spiritualem corporis Christi tàm præsentiam quam participationem pleno ore confessurus, in Responsione ad priorem Imperatoris quæstionem: Num Mysteriôso quôdam modô corpus Christi in Cœna à Fidelibus sumatur? occupatus, inter alia ita respondet: Quandoquidem omnium confessione corpus & sanguis Christi in Cœna sumitur, necesse est, panem & vinum in melius quoddam transiisse, mutationemque hanc non CORPORALITER, sed SPIRITUALITER contigisse, ut jam nunc rectè dicatur, mutationem dictam FIGURATIVE factam esse, subque tegumento corporalis panis & vini, SPIRITUALE CORPUS ET SPIRITUALEM SANGUINEM Christi, actu præsentem esse… Quoniam est SPIRITUALIS ESCA, est SPIRITUALIS POTUS, spiritualiter pascens & æternæ satietatis vitam tribuens.
